searchText: Fast is always ideal 😉 So i guess upper limit is below 10s magnitude Yeah I think that’s fair but I’d likely still complain it’s slow and for cases that need eth_getProof suggest another client. I’m quite happy to see clients leverage different designs to provide different trade offs though. In this case you could make getProof a lot faster by storing all trie nodes but then you use a lot more disk (and have other challenges with handling that much data). I like giving users the ability to pick a client that makes trade offs that match their needs. Yeah so I am not making a 10TB archive node for something that people have been rarely asking us at best It seems that even for wallets almost noone has complained about us not supporting it, most come from people running op nodes and it happens quite rarely I am planning to make a flag for it tho and not make that default It comes with many challenges still but i think it is doable to allow optional say 500 GBs with 0.5-3s response time for people that want all trie nodes history I would imagine wallets generally only care about things at or near the tip so not surprising it isn’t a huge use case. There is a big element here of how much you trust the source node though. Generally op-node is very paranoid about its source node because there’s been plenty of wrong responses received from various api providers and nodes for different reasons. As you move more to light nodes being able to prove responses are correct becomes more useful as well. Definitely like the idea of an optional extra storage to accelerate things. is this why you guys have the trust l1 rpc flag on by default? Yes, it is just that most people do not particularly care of getProof and most rpc providers block it because it is problematic amyway Yeah trust rpc is false by default and we verify the responses (which includes using getProof when accessing storage values from L1) I don’t recall encountering an rpc provider that blocks eth_getProof. I’ve heard that mentioned a bunch but don’t think I’ve ever encountered it. It is common to limit all requests that need an archive node to paid plans though. infura and ankr do Portal network should be serving `eth_getProof` from 21million -> HEAD by Q2 2025. Likely full archive by end of 2025. You can do anything up to block 1 million live on the network today. this is also something I am considering. make it reaaallly fast but only for last few millions blocks this is a tradeoff-space of disk and response time Infura have supported eth_getProof for years - not sure it was ever not supported (though I have heard people claim that before). https://docs.metamask.io/services/reference/optimism/json-rpc-methods/eth_getproof/ I’m. It entirely sure why docs.infura.io is redirecting to docs.metamask.io mind you. i heard it did not but maybe i am wrong i did hear by others (e.g ankr to name one), it has always been a tricky one

excerpts.author: funnygiulio
excerpts.content: Fast is always ideal 😉

excerpts.author: funnygiulio
excerpts.content: So i guess upper limit is below 10s magnitude

excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content:
Yeah I think that’s fair but I’d likely still complain it’s slow and for cases that need eth_getProof suggest another client. 
I’m quite happy to see clients leverage different designs to provide different trade offs though. In this case you could make getProof a lot faster by storing all trie nodes but then you use a lot more disk (and have other challenges with handling that much data). I like giving users the ability to pick a client that makes trade offs that match their needs.

excerpts.author: funnygiulio
excerpts.content: It comes with many challenges still but i think it is doable to allow optional say 500 GBs with 0.5-3s response time for people that want all trie nodes history

excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content:
I would imagine wallets generally only care about things at or near the tip so not surprising it isn’t a huge use case. 
There is a big element here of how much you trust the source node though. Generally op-node is very paranoid about its source node because there’s been plenty of wrong responses received from various api providers and nodes for different reasons. As you move more to light nodes being able to prove responses are correct becomes more useful as well.

excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content: Definitely like the idea of an optional extra storage to accelerate things.

excerpts.author: funnygiulio
excerpts.content: is this why you guys have the trust l1 rpc flag on by default?

excerpts.content: Yes, it is just that most people do not particularly care of getProof and most rpc providers block it because it is problematic amyway

excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content: Yeah trust rpc is false by default and we verify the responses (which includes using getProof when accessing storage values from L1)

excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content: I don’t recall encountering an rpc provider that blocks eth_getProof. I’ve heard that mentioned a bunch but don’t think I’ve ever encountered it. It is common to limit all requests that need an archive node to paid plans though.
